Module 1: Introduction & Setup (30 minutes)

Learning Objectives

  • Understand what Amazon Q Developer is and how it supports SAP ABAP
  • Set up the complete development environment from scratch
  • Choose your preferred IDE: VS Code, Kiro, or Eclipse (SAP ADT)

Reference Workshop: For additional visual guidance with screenshots, see the official AWS workshop: Amazon Q Developer for SAP ABAP on Eclipse

1.1 What is Amazon Q Developer?

Amazon Q Developer is a generative AI-powered assistant that helps developers build, transform, and operate applications on AWS. It works across the full SAP programming spectrum — classical ABAP, the ABAP RESTful Application Programming Model (RAP), and the SAP Cloud Application Programming Model (CAP) — and is available as an IDE extension in VS Code, Eclipse, and more. For SAP ABAP developers pursuing SAP's recommended clean core strategy, it provides:

  • Clean core development — Generate RAP/CAP artifacts and side-by-side extensions that keep the digital core standard and upgrade-stable
  • Code generation — Write ABAP code (and full Fiori/BTP apps) from natural language descriptions
  • Code explanation — Understand legacy ABAP programs instantly
  • Code transformation — Modernize classical ABAP toward ABAP Cloud and released APIs
  • Debugging assistance — Identify and fix runtime errors and performance issues
  • Documentation — Auto-generate functional and technical documentation

What is "clean core"? SAP's clean core strategy keeps the SAP S/4HANA digital core close to standard and upgrade-stable across six dimensions — software stack, extensibility, integrations, processes, data, and operations. Instead of modifying the core, you extend SAP through released APIs, CDS/RAP, and side-by-side (BTP) or on-stack (ABAP Cloud) extensions. This makes upgrades cheaper, faster, and cloud-compliant. Amazon Q Developer accelerates the code-level work of getting and staying clean core.

1.2 What is Kiro?

Kiro is an agentic AI IDE from AWS that goes beyond code completion. It uses spec-driven development to turn natural language prompts into structured requirements, system designs, and implementation tasks. Key features:

  • Spec-driven development — Turns prompts into requirements, design, and tasks before writing code
  • Agent hooks — Automate tasks like generating docs and tests on file save
  • Steering files — Configure clean core standards and preferred workflows per project
  • Built on Code OSS — Familiar VS Code experience, import your existing settings and extensions
  • Native MCP support — Connect to SAP directly (e.g., the AWS ABAP Accelerator MCP server) to read code, validate against ATC, and generate clean core artifacts

1.3 Supported ABAP Patterns

Amazon Q and Kiro understand: - Classical ABAP (reports, module pools, function modules) - ABAP Objects (classes, interfaces) - CDS views and ABAP annotations - RAP (RESTful ABAP Programming Model) — the clean core, on-stack extension model - CAP (Cloud Application Programming Model) — for side-by-side extensions on SAP BTP - ALV programming (classical and OO) - SAP-specific tables, BAPIs, released APIs, and transactions

1.4 Choose Your IDE

Feature VS Code + Amazon Q Kiro Eclipse (SAP ADT) + Amazon Q
AI Chat & Code Suggestions
Spec-Driven Development
Agent Hooks (auto-tasks)
Native SAP System Connection
CDS View Editor Via extensions Via extensions Native
ABAP Debugger Native
Transport Management Native
Price Free tier Free tier Free (Eclipse + ADT)

Recommendation: - Choose Option A (VS Code) for a lightweight setup focused on AI-assisted coding - Choose Option B (Kiro) for the full agentic AI experience with spec-driven development - Choose Option C (Eclipse/ADT) if you need direct SAP system connection, debugging, and transport management — best for on-premise SAP developers

Hands-On Lab 1B.3: Configure Kiro for ABAP Development

Step 1: Create a steering file for ABAP standards

  1. Open your project folder in Kiro
  2. Create .kiro/steering/abap.md with this content:
# ABAP Clean Core Development Standards

## Clean Core Principles
- Never modify SAP standard objects — extend, don't modify
- Consume RELEASED APIs and released CDS views only (check the API state)
- Prefer on-stack extensions with ABAP Cloud / RAP, or side-by-side on SAP BTP (CAP)
- Keep the digital core upgrade-stable and cloud-compliant

## Coding Standards
- Follow Clean ABAP guidelines
- Use modern ABAP syntax (inline declarations, string templates, NEW operator)
- No SELECT * — always use explicit field lists
- No SELECT inside LOOP — use JOINs or FOR ALL ENTRIES
- Use CL_SALV_TABLE for ALV output (not REUSE_ALV_*)
- Use RETURNING parameters instead of CHANGING where possible

## Naming Conventions
- Local variables: lv_, lt_, ls_, lo_, lr_, lx_
- Global variables: gv_, gt_, gs_, go_
- Parameters: iv_, it_, is_, io_ (importing), ev_, et_ (exporting), rv_, rt_ (returning)
- Classes: zcl_ prefix
- Interfaces: zif_ prefix

## SAP Version
- Target: S/4HANA 2023 or later (Cloud Private or Public Edition)
- Use released APIs where possible for clean core compliance

Kiro — File Explorer
project/
└─ .kiro/steering/abap.md

Module 2: ABAP Code Generation with Amazon Q (45 minutes)

Learning Objectives

  • Generate ABAP code using natural language prompts
  • Use inline code suggestions for ABAP development
  • Understand how to write effective prompts for ABAP

Warm-Up Exercise (2 minutes)

Before we start the real labs, let's build confidence with a simple prompt. Copy and paste this into your chat:

Write a simple ABAP report that prints "Hello, Amazon Q!" to the screen. Use modern ABAP syntax.
Expected: You should get a short report with WRITE or cl_demo_output
If you get stuck: This is just a warm-up. If it doesn't work, check your connection in Module 1. You can skip ahead and come back.

2.1 Prompting Strategies for ABAP

Effective prompts for ABAP code generation should include:

  1. Context — SAP module (MM, SD, FI), system version (ECC, S/4HANA)
  2. Specifics — Table names, field names, transaction codes
  3. Standards — Clean ABAP, naming conventions, modern syntax
  4. Output format — Report, class, CDS view, function module

Good vs. Bad Prompts

Vague Prompt Specific Prompt
Write code to read purchase orders Write an ABAP report that reads purchase orders from EKKO/EKPO, filters by company code (BUKRS) and creation date (AEDAT) using selection screen parameters, and displays results in an ALV grid using CL_SALV_TABLE
Create a CDS view for sales Create a CDS view entity joining VBAK and VBAP with associations to I_BusinessPartner and I_Product, exposing sales order number, item, material, quantity, net value, and currency

Hands-On Lab 2.1: Generate an ALV Report

Instructions

  1. Open the Amazon Q chat panel
  2. Enter the following prompt:
Write an ABAP report that:
- Has a selection screen with parameters for company code (BUKRS) and
  a select-option for document date (AEDAT)
- Reads purchase order headers (EKKO) and items (EKPO) using a JOIN
- Displays results in an ALV grid using CL_SALV_TABLE
- Uses modern ABAP syntax (inline declarations, string templates)
- Follows Clean ABAP naming conventions
  1. Review the generated code
  2. Copy it into your ABAP project
  3. Verify the structure includes:
  4. Selection screen definition
  5. Data retrieval with JOIN
  6. ALV display using CL_SALV_TABLE
  7. Inline declarations (DATA(...))
  8. Proper error handling

Expected Output Structure

REPORT z_po_alv_report.

" Selection screen
PARAMETERS: p_bukrs TYPE bukrs OBLIGATORY.
SELECT-OPTIONS: s_aedat FOR sy-datum.

START-OF-SELECTION.

  " Data retrieval with JOIN
  SELECT e~ebeln, e~bukrs, e~aedat, e~lifnr,
         p~ebelp, p~matnr, p~menge, p~netpr
    FROM ekko AS e
    INNER JOIN ekpo AS p ON e~ebeln = p~ebeln
    WHERE e~bukrs = @p_bukrs
      AND e~aedat IN @s_aedat
    INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_po_data).

  " ALV display
  TRY.
      cl_salv_table=>factory(
        IMPORTING r_salv_table = DATA(lo_alv)
        CHANGING  t_table      = lt_po_data ).
      lo_alv->display( ).
    CATCH cx_salv_msg INTO DATA(lx_msg).
      MESSAGE lx_msg->get_text( ) TYPE 'E'.
  ENDTRY.

Instructions

Create an ABAP CDS view entity called Z_I_SalesOrderItem that:

  and I_Material (via VBAP-MATNR)
- Has proper annotations for metadata and UI

  3. @AbapCatalog annotations
  4. @ObjectModel annotations
  5. Proper JOIN syntax
  6. Association definitions
  7. Field aliases with proper naming

Hands-On Lab 2.3: Generate a RAP Business Object

Instructions

  1. Enter the following prompt:
Generate a managed RAP business object for a travel booking app with:
- Root entity: Travel (travel_id, agency_id, customer_id, begin_date,
  end_date, total_price, currency_code, status)
- Include: CDS view entity, behavior definition, behavior implementation class,
  and service definition/binding
- Use draft handling and managed numbering
- Add validations for date consistency (begin_date < end_date)

  2. CDS view entity
  3. Behavior definition (BDEF)

Hands-On Lab 2.4: Generate a Draw.io Architecture Diagram

Amazon Q can also generate draw.io XML that you can import directly into diagrams.net (draw.io) to visualize your ABAP architecture.

Instructions

  1. Enter the following refined prompt (save this!):
Generate a draw.io file (.drawio XML format) and save it to [your-path]/sap-sales-order-flow.drawio. The diagram should show the architecture of a sales order flow with these components and numbered flow:

1. User triggers sales order creation via Fiori app
2. Fiori app calls OData service (RAP-based)
3. RAP Business Object: ZI_SalesOrder (CDS + BDEF + behavior implementation as sub-components)
4. Behavior implementation calls BAPI_SALESORDER_CREATEFROMDAT2 via RFC wrapper
5. BAPI writes to VBAK/VBAP tables (cylinder shapes)
6. A background job reads new orders and sends IDoc to external system
7. Amazon Q Developer shown as a side panel with capabilities (code gen, explain, debug, modernize, test)

Include a color legend.

Color scheme:
- Fiori/UI layer: #0070F2 (SAP blue)
- RAP/OData layer: #FF9900 (AWS orange)
- Database layer: #1B660F (green)
- External systems: #879596 (gray)
- Amazon Q panel: #232F3E background with #FF9900 accent

Use layer background rectangles, numbered arrows between components, and orthogonal edge routing. Output as a complete .drawio file I can open directly.
  1. Save the generated XML as sap-sales-order-flow.drawio
  2. Open it in app.diagrams.net (File → Open) or double-click the .drawio file

Example Output

Here's what the generated diagram looks like — with layered architecture, numbered flow arrows, color-coded components, and a legend:

sap-sales-order-flow.drawio — Generated by Amazon Q Developer

⬆ This diagram was generated entirely by AI from the prompt above. Colors, layout, numbered arrows, sub-components, cylinder shapes for DB tables, and the legend — all from a single prompt.

Expected: A layered architecture diagram with Fiori (blue), RAP (orange), Database (green), External (gray) layers, numbered arrows 1-7, cylinder shapes for VBAK/VBAP, Amazon Q panel with capabilities, and a color legend
Try more diagram prompts:
Generate a draw.io XML diagram showing the CDS view hierarchy for a purchase order reporting scenario:
- Top level: ZC_PurchaseOrder (consumption view, OData exposed)
- Middle: ZI_PurchaseOrder (interface view, joins EKKO + EKPO)
- Base: EKKO, EKPO, LFA1 (database tables)
- Show associations with arrows and cardinality labels (1:N, 1:1)
Output only raw XML.
Generate a draw.io XML sequence diagram showing:
1. User opens Fiori app
2. Fiori sends OData request to SAP Gateway
3. Gateway calls RAP handler
4. RAP handler calls CDS view
5. CDS view reads from HANA database
6. Response flows back through each layer
Use SAP-style colors and include timing annotations.
Output only raw XML.
Tip: If the diagram doesn't look right, ask a follow-up: "Rearrange the boxes so the flow goes top-to-bottom. Make the boxes wider and add more spacing." You can iterate until it looks good.

Tips

  • Use follow-up prompts to refine: "Add sorting by document date descending"
  • Ask for variations: "Now make a version that uses ABAP Cloud released APIs only"
  • Request explanations: "Explain why you used CL_SALV_TABLE instead of REUSE_ALV_GRID_DISPLAY"
  • Generate diagrams: "Create a draw.io XML showing the data flow for this report"

Checkpoint

  • Successfully generated an ALV report
  • Generated a CDS view with associations
  • Generated RAP business object artifacts
  • Generated a draw.io architecture diagram
  • Understand how prompt specificity affects output quality

Module 3: ABAP Code Explanation & Documentation (30 minutes)

Learning Objectives

  • Use Amazon Q to explain legacy ABAP code
  • Generate documentation for existing programs

3.1 Why Code Explanation Matters

SAP systems often contain decades of custom ABAP code with: - Minimal or outdated documentation - Complex business logic embedded in nested loops - Dynamic programming (field symbols, ASSIGN, GENERATE SUBROUTINE POOL) - Implicit dependencies on SAP standard behavior

Amazon Q can analyze ABAP code and explain the business logic, data flow, and potential issues.

Hands-On Lab 3.1: Explain Legacy Code

Instructions

  1. Copy the following legacy ABAP code into your editor or the Amazon Q chat:
REPORT z_legacy_sales_report.

TABLES: vbak, vbap, kna1.

DATA: lt_vbak TYPE TABLE OF vbak,
      ls_vbak TYPE vbak,
      lt_vbap TYPE TABLE OF vbap,
      ls_vbap TYPE vbap,
      lv_total TYPE vbap-netwr,
      lv_count TYPE i,
      lt_kna1 TYPE HASHED TABLE OF kna1 WITH UNIQUE KEY kunnr.

SELECT-OPTIONS: s_erdat FOR vbak-erdat,
                s_vkorg FOR vbak-vkorg.

START-OF-SELECTION.

SELECT * FROM vbak INTO TABLE lt_vbak
  WHERE erdat IN s_erdat
    AND vkorg IN s_vkorg
    AND vbtyp = 'C'.

IF lt_vbak IS NOT INITIAL.
  SELECT * FROM kna1 INTO TABLE lt_kna1
    FOR ALL ENTRIES IN lt_vbak
    WHERE kunnr = lt_vbak-kunnr.
ENDIF.

LOOP AT lt_vbak INTO ls_vbak.
  SELECT * FROM vbap INTO TABLE lt_vbap
    WHERE vbeln = ls_vbak-vbeln.
  CLEAR lv_total.
  LOOP AT lt_vbap INTO ls_vbap.
    lv_total = lv_total + ls_vbap-netwr.
    lv_count = lv_count + 1.
  ENDLOOP.
  READ TABLE lt_kna1 INTO DATA(ls_kna1)
    WITH TABLE KEY kunnr = ls_vbak-kunnr.
  WRITE: / ls_vbak-vbeln, ls_vbak-erdat, ls_kna1-name1, lv_total, lv_count.
  CLEAR lv_count.
ENDLOOP.
  1. Ask Amazon Q:
Explain this ABAP code in detail. Describe:
1. The business purpose
2. The data flow
3. Any performance issues
4. Suggestions for improvement
  1. Review the explanation and verify Amazon Q identifies:
  2. The report reads sales orders (VBTYP = 'C') filtered by date and sales org
  3. It performs a nested SELECT inside a LOOP (N+1 query problem)
  4. Customer names are fetched using a hashed table (good pattern)
  5. The WRITE statement outputs a flat list
  6. Performance issue: SELECT inside LOOP for VBAP

Hands-On Lab 3.3: Explain Dynamic ABAP Code

  1. Ask Amazon Q to explain this dynamic programming pattern:
FIELD-SYMBOLS: <lt_table> TYPE STANDARD TABLE,
               <ls_line>  TYPE any,
               <lv_field> TYPE any.

DATA: lo_descr  TYPE REF TO cl_abap_structdescr,
      lt_comp   TYPE abap_compdescr_tab,
      lr_data   TYPE REF TO data.

lo_descr ?= cl_abap_typedescr=>describe_by_name( iv_table_name ).
lt_comp = lo_descr->components.

CREATE DATA lr_data TYPE TABLE OF (iv_table_name).
ASSIGN lr_data->* TO <lt_table>.

SELECT * FROM (iv_table_name) INTO TABLE <lt_table> UP TO 100 ROWS.

LOOP AT <lt_table> ASSIGNING <ls_line>.
  LOOP AT lt_comp INTO DATA(ls_comp).
    ASSIGN COMPONENT ls_comp-name OF STRUCTURE <ls_line> TO <lv_field>.
    WRITE: / ls_comp-name, ':', <lv_field>.
  ENDLOOP.
ENDLOOP.
  1. Prompt:
Explain this dynamic ABAP code. What does it do, and what are the
security implications of using dynamic table names?

Module 4: Clean Core Modernization & Refactoring (45 minutes)

Learning Objectives

  • Understand SAP's clean core strategy and its six dimensions
  • Modernize legacy ABAP toward clean core: Clean ABAP, released APIs, and ABAP Cloud
  • Refactor classical patterns to modern, upgrade-stable equivalents

4.0 The Clean Core Strategy

Clean core is SAP's framework of best practices for keeping SAP S/4HANA (Cloud Private or Public Edition) and its extensions upgrade-stable and cloud-compliant. The core principle: extend SAP to meet your unique requirements without modifying the core application. A clean core improves performance across six dimensions:

Dimension What "clean" means Where Amazon Q helps
Software stack Stay close to standard; no modifications to SAP objects Refactor mods into released extension points
Extensibility Use released APIs, ABAP Cloud/RAP (on-stack) or BTP/CAP (side-by-side) Generate RAP/CAP artifacts and released-API code
Integrations API-led, event-driven, standard integration scenarios Generate OData/REST integration code
Data Clean, high-quality master data; archiving Explain data flows, spot quality issues
Processes Standard processes, minimal custom logic Assess and simplify custom code
Operations Streamlined, monitorable, low-risk operations Analyze dumps, optimize performance

Why it matters: Heavy core customization makes upgrades slow, risky, and expensive. Clean core keeps you current with new SAP features at lower cost. This module focuses on the software stack and extensibility dimensions — the code-level work of getting clean.

4.1 Modernization Targets

Legacy Pattern Modern Replacement
DATA: lv_var TYPE ... DATA(lv_var) = ... (inline declaration)
CONCATENATE a b INTO c c = \|{ a }{ b }\| (string templates)
CREATE OBJECT lo_obj lo_obj = NEW #( )
CALL METHOD lo_obj->method lo_obj->method( )
MOVE a TO b b = a
SELECT * FROM ... SELECT field1, field2 FROM ...
REUSE_ALV_GRID_DISPLAY CL_SALV_TABLE
READ TABLE ... WITH KEY READ TABLE ... WITH TABLE KEY or line_exists( )
Header lines Explicit work areas
FORM/PERFORM Methods in classes

4.2 Clean ABAP Principles

  • Use meaningful names (no Hungarian notation for local variables)
  • Keep methods small and focused
  • Prefer functional over procedural style
  • Use exceptions instead of return codes
  • Avoid deep nesting

Hands-On Lab 4.1: Modernize the Legacy Report

- Use string templates instead of WRITE

- Use modern ABAP syntax (NEW, VALUE, CORRESPONDING, etc.)
- Add proper error handling with TRY/CATCH

Expected Transformation

Before: ~40 lines, 3 separate SELECTs (one inside a loop), WRITE output After: ~30 lines, single JOIN query, CL_SALV_TABLE output, inline declarations

Module 5: Debugging & Troubleshooting ABAP with Amazon Q (30 minutes)

Learning Objectives

  • Use Amazon Q to identify and fix ABAP runtime errors
  • Troubleshoot common SAP issues
  • Optimize ABAP performance

5.1 Common ABAP Issues Amazon Q Can Help With

Issue Type Examples
Runtime errors GETWA_NOT_ASSIGNED, ITAB_DUPLICATE_KEY, COMPUTE_INT_ZERODIVIDE
Performance SELECT in LOOP, missing indexes, large internal tables
Type mismatches Incompatible types in assignments, conversions
Logic errors Incorrect loop processing, missing CLEAR statements
Authorization Missing authority checks, SY-SUBRC handling

Hands-On Lab 5.1: Fix a Buggy Program

Instructions

  1. Review this ABAP program that contains multiple issues:
REPORT z_buggy_program.

DATA: lt_items TYPE TABLE OF vbap,
      lt_materials TYPE TABLE OF mara,
      lv_total TYPE p DECIMALS 2.

" Issue 1: SELECT * without WHERE - reads entire table
SELECT * FROM vbap INTO TABLE lt_items.

" Issue 2: SELECT inside LOOP (N+1 problem)
LOOP AT lt_items INTO DATA(ls_item).
  SELECT SINGLE * FROM mara INTO @DATA(ls_mara)
    WHERE matnr = @ls_item-matnr.

  " Issue 3: No SY-SUBRC check after SELECT SINGLE
  lv_total = lv_total + ls_item-netwr * ls_mara-ntgew.

  " Issue 4: READ TABLE without TRANSPORTING NO FIELDS for existence check
  READ TABLE lt_items INTO DATA(ls_check)
    WITH KEY vbeln = ls_item-vbeln
             posnr = ls_item-posnr.
ENDLOOP.

" Issue 5: Division without zero check
DATA(lv_avg) = lv_total / lines( lt_items ).

WRITE: / 'Average:', lv_avg.
  1. Ask Amazon Q:
This ABAP program has multiple bugs and performance issues.
Identify all issues and provide a corrected version.
  1. Verify Amazon Q identifies all 5 issues:
  2. SELECT * without WHERE clause
  3. SELECT inside LOOP
  4. Missing SY-SUBRC check
  5. Inefficient READ TABLE
  6. Division by zero risk

Hands-On Lab 5.2: Analyze an ABAP Dump

Instructions

  1. Simulate an ST22 dump analysis by providing this error context to Amazon Q:
I got this ABAP runtime error in production:

Runtime Error: GETWA_NOT_ASSIGNED
Program: Z_PROCESS_ORDERS
Include: Z_PROCESS_ORDERS
Line: 42

Source code extract:
  FIELD-SYMBOLS: <ls_order> TYPE ty_order.
  READ TABLE lt_orders ASSIGNING <ls_order>
    WITH KEY order_id = lv_order_id.
  <ls_order>-status = 'COMPLETED'.    " <-- Line 42

The error occurs intermittently, only for certain order IDs.
What is the cause and how do I fix it?
  1. Verify Amazon Q explains:
  2. The field symbol is not assigned because READ TABLE didn't find a match
  3. SY-SUBRC check is missing after READ TABLE
  4. The fix: add IF sy-subrc = 0 or IF <ls_order> IS ASSIGNED

Hands-On Lab 5.3: Performance Optimization

Instructions

  1. Provide this slow-performing code:
" This report takes 30+ minutes to run in production
LOOP AT lt_sales_orders INTO DATA(ls_so).
  LOOP AT lt_deliveries INTO DATA(ls_del)
    WHERE vbeln = ls_so-vbeln.
    LOOP AT lt_billing INTO DATA(ls_bill)
      WHERE vbeln = ls_del-vbeln.
      SELECT SINGLE * FROM bsad INTO @DATA(ls_cleared)
        WHERE bukrs = @ls_bill-bukrs
          AND belnr = @ls_bill-belnr.
      IF sy-subrc = 0.
        APPEND VALUE #(
          vbeln = ls_so-vbeln
          del_no = ls_del-vbeln
          bill_no = ls_bill-vbeln
          cleared = abap_true
        ) TO lt_result.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.
  ENDLOOP.
ENDLOOP.
  1. Prompt:
This ABAP code takes 30+ minutes in production. Analyze the performance
issues and rewrite it to run efficiently. Explain each optimization.
  1. Expected optimizations Amazon Q should suggest:
  2. Replace nested LOOPs with sorted/hashed tables or secondary keys
  3. Move SELECT out of the loop — use FOR ALL ENTRIES or JOIN
  4. Consider using a single JOIN query to replace the entire nested structure
  5. Use PARALLEL CURSOR technique if nested LOOPs are necessary

Checkpoint

  • Identified and fixed multiple bugs in ABAP code
  • Analyzed a simulated ABAP dump
  • Optimized a slow-performing ABAP program

6.1 Use Case: S/4HANA Migration Preparation

Scenario

Your organization is migrating from ECC 6.0 to S/4HANA. You have 500+ custom ABAP programs that need compatibility assessment.

Lab Exercise

  1. Provide code that uses deprecated APIs:
" Uses direct BSEG access (not recommended in S/4HANA)
SELECT * FROM bseg INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_bseg)
  WHERE bukrs = @p_bukrs
    AND belnr = @p_belnr
    AND gjahr = @p_gjahr.

" Uses KONV direct access (replaced in S/4HANA)
SELECT * FROM konv INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_konv)
  WHERE knumv = @lv_knumv.

" Uses obsolete BDC approach
CALL TRANSACTION 'VA01' USING lt_bdcdata MODE 'N'.
  1. Prompt:
This ABAP code needs to be migrated to S/4HANA. Identify all
incompatible or deprecated patterns and provide S/4HANA-compatible
replacements. Reference the SAP simplification list where applicable.

6.4 Use Case: Unit Testing

Lab Exercise

6.5 Best Practices Summary

Effective Prompting for ABAP

Aspect Recommendation
SAP Module Specify: MM, SD, FI, PP, etc.
System Version State: ECC 6.0, S/4HANA 2023, ABAP Cloud
Tables/Objects Name specific tables, BAPIs, function modules
Coding Standard Request: Clean ABAP, naming conventions
Error Context Include dump details, error messages, SY-SUBRC values
Output Format Specify: report, class, CDS view, RAP BO

When Amazon Q Works Best

  • Generating boilerplate code (ALV, CDS, RAP, selection screens)
  • Explaining unfamiliar legacy code
  • Modernizing syntax patterns
  • Identifying common bugs and performance issues
  • Generating unit test scaffolding

When to Verify Carefully

  • Business logic specific to your organization
  • SAP table relationships and field semantics
  • Authorization concepts and security-critical code
  • System-specific customizing dependencies

Wrap-Up

Key Takeaways

  1. Amazon Q Developer accelerates ABAP development across the full lifecycle
  2. Prompt quality directly impacts output quality — be specific
  3. Always review and test generated code before deploying
  4. Combine AI assistance with SAP domain expertise for best results

Lab 3.1: Explain Legacy Code

Objective

Steps

REPORT z_legacy_sales_report.

TABLES: vbak, vbap, kna1.

DATA: lt_vbak TYPE TABLE OF vbak,

  WRITE: / ls_vbak-vbeln, ls_vbak-erdat, ls_kna1-name1, lv_total, lv_count.
  CLEAR lv_count.
ENDLOOP.

ENDFORM.
  1. Prompt:
Convert these FORM routines into a proper ABAP OO class with methods.
Follow Clean ABAP guidelines, use RETURNING parameters where possible,
and add appropriate exception handling.
  1. Verify the output:
  2. Class definition with proper visibility sections
  3. RETURNING parameters instead of CHANGING where possible
  4. Exception class for error handling
  5. No FORM/PERFORM statements remain

Lab Instructions — Module 5: Debugging & Troubleshooting

Lab 5.1: Fix a Buggy Program

Time: 10 minutes

Objective

Use Amazon Q to identify and fix multiple issues in an ABAP program.

Steps

  1. Provide this buggy code to Amazon Q:
REPORT z_buggy_program.

DATA: lt_items TYPE TABLE OF vbap,
      lt_materials TYPE TABLE OF mara,
      lv_total TYPE p DECIMALS 2.

" Issue 1: SELECT * without WHERE - reads entire table
SELECT * FROM vbap INTO TABLE lt_items.

" Issue 2: SELECT inside LOOP (N+1 problem)
LOOP AT lt_items INTO DATA(ls_item).
  SELECT SINGLE * FROM mara INTO @DATA(ls_mara)
    WHERE matnr = @ls_item-matnr.

  " Issue 3: No SY-SUBRC check after SELECT SINGLE
  lv_total = lv_total + ls_item-netwr * ls_mara-ntgew.

  " Issue 4: READ TABLE without TRANSPORTING NO FIELDS for existence check
  READ TABLE lt_items INTO DATA(ls_check)
    WITH KEY vbeln = ls_item-vbeln
             posnr = ls_item-posnr.
ENDLOOP.

" Issue 5: Division without zero check
DATA(lv_avg) = lv_total / lines( lt_items ).

WRITE: / 'Average:', lv_avg.
  1. Prompt:
This ABAP program has multiple bugs and performance issues.
Identify all issues and provide a corrected version.
  1. Verify Amazon Q finds all 5 issues:
  2. Issue 1: SELECT * without WHERE reads entire VBAP table
  3. Issue 2: SELECT SINGLE inside LOOP (N+1 query)
  4. Issue 3: No SY-SUBRC check — ls_mara may have initial values
  5. Issue 4: READ TABLE copies data unnecessarily
  6. Issue 5: Division by zero if lt_items is empty

Lab 5.2: Analyze an ABAP Dump

Time: 10 minutes

Objective

Use Amazon Q to diagnose a runtime error from ST22.

Steps

  1. Provide this dump context:
I got this ABAP runtime error in production:

Runtime Error: GETWA_NOT_ASSIGNED
Program: Z_PROCESS_ORDERS
Include: Z_PROCESS_ORDERS
Line: 42

Source code extract:
  FIELD-SYMBOLS: <ls_order> TYPE ty_order.
  READ TABLE lt_orders ASSIGNING <ls_order>
    WITH KEY order_id = lv_order_id.
  <ls_order>-status = 'COMPLETED'.    " <-- Line 42

The error occurs intermittently, only for certain order IDs.
What is the cause and how do I fix it?
  1. Verify the response explains:
  2. READ TABLE didn't find a matching entry
  3. Field symbol <ls_order> is unassigned
  4. Accessing an unassigned field symbol causes the dump
  5. Fix: check IF sy-subrc = 0 or IF <ls_order> IS ASSIGNED

Lab 5.3: Performance Optimization

Time: 10 minutes

Objective

Optimize a slow-running ABAP program with Amazon Q's help.

Steps

  1. Provide this code:
" This report takes 30+ minutes to run in production
LOOP AT lt_sales_orders INTO DATA(ls_so).
  LOOP AT lt_deliveries INTO DATA(ls_del)
    WHERE vbeln = ls_so-vbeln.
    LOOP AT lt_billing INTO DATA(ls_bill)
      WHERE vbeln = ls_del-vbeln.
      SELECT SINGLE * FROM bsad INTO @DATA(ls_cleared)
        WHERE bukrs = @ls_bill-bukrs
          AND belnr = @ls_bill-belnr.
      IF sy-subrc = 0.
        APPEND VALUE #(
          vbeln = ls_so-vbeln
          del_no = ls_del-vbeln
          bill_no = ls_bill-vbeln
          cleared = abap_true
        ) TO lt_result.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.
  ENDLOOP.
ENDLOOP.
  1. Prompt:
This ABAP code takes 30+ minutes in production. Analyze the performance
issues and rewrite it to run efficiently. Explain each optimization.
  1. Expected optimizations:
  2. Replace nested LOOPs with sorted tables or secondary keys
  3. Move SELECT out of loop — use FOR ALL ENTRIES or JOIN
  4. Consider replacing entire structure with a single SQL JOIN
  5. Use parallel cursor technique if nested LOOPs remain

Lab Instructions — MCP for SAP ABAP

Estimated time: 20–25 minutes
If you get stuck: Skip this lab and move to the next one. You can always come back later. The labs are independent of each other.

Lab MCP.1: Install and Connect the MCP Server

Time: 10 minutes

Objective

Install an SAP ABAP MCP server and connect it to your IDE so Amazon Q / Kiro can read SAP objects directly.

Prerequisites

  • Python 3.9+ installed (python3 --version to check)
  • Access to an SAP system with ADT services enabled
  • SAP username, password, client number, and system URL

Steps

Step 1 — Clone and install the MCP server:

git clone https://github.com/YahorNovik/mcp-adt.git
cd mcp-adt
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

Step 2 — Create the SAP connection file:

# Create .env file in the mcp-adt folder
cat > .env << 'EOF'
SAP_AUTH_TYPE=basic
SAP_URL=https://your-sap-system:443
SAP_CLIENT=100
SAP_USER=your_username
SAP_PASS=your_password
SAP_VERIFY_SSL=true
EOF
Replace the placeholder values with your actual SAP credentials. Never commit this file to Git.

Step 3 — Test the connection:

# Quick test — should return XML if connection works
curl -u your_username:your_password https://your-sap-system:443/sap/bc/adt/discovery

Step 4 — Add to your IDE:

For VS Code + Amazon Q:

# Add to ~/.aws/amazonq/default.json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "sap-abap-adt": {
      "command": "python3",
      "args": ["/full/path/to/mcp-adt/mcp_server.py"],
      "timeout": 60
    }
  }
}

For Kiro:

# Add to ~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "sap-abap-adt": {
      "command": "python3",
      "args": ["/full/path/to/mcp-adt/mcp_server.py"],
      "timeout": 60
    }
  }
}

Verification

  • Open the chat panel in your IDE
  • Check the MCP tools icon — you should see sap-abap-adt listed as connected
  • If you see a red error, click "Fix Configuration" and check your path and .env file
Expected: MCP server shows as "Connected" with 15+ tools available

Lab MCP.2: Read SAP Objects via Chat

Time: 5 minutes

Objective

Use natural language prompts to read ABAP source code and table definitions directly from SAP — without copy-pasting.

Exercise A — Read a program

Type this in your AI chat:

Read the source code of the ABAP demo program SAPBC_DATA_GENERATOR and explain what it does.
Expected: The AI calls get_program_source, retrieves the code, and gives you a summary — all without you pasting anything

Exercise B — Explore a table structure

Get the structure of table SCARR (airline carriers). Then write a modern ABAP SELECT that reads all carriers and displays them in an ALV grid.
Expected: The AI calls get_table_source for SCARR, sees the fields (CARRID, CARRNAME, CURRCODE, URL), and generates a working ABAP report

Exercise C — Read table data

Show me the first 5 rows from table SCARR.
Expected: The AI calls get_table_contents with max_rows=5 and shows you actual data like AA/American Airlines, LH/Lufthansa, etc.

Lab MCP.3: Advanced — Where-Used and Cross-Object Analysis

Time: 10 minutes

Objective

Use MCP tools for cross-object analysis that would normally require multiple SAP transactions.

Exercise A — Where-used analysis

Find all objects that reference function module POPUP_TO_CONFIRM. List the top 5 and explain how each one uses it.
Expected: The AI calls get_usage_references and returns a list of programs/classes that call this FM, with context on each usage

Exercise B — Search and compare

Search for all ABAP objects matching "SFLIGHT*". Then read the source of program SAPBC_DATA_GENERATOR and the structure of table SFLIGHT. Explain how they relate to each other.
Expected: The AI chains multiple MCP calls — search_objects, get_program_source, get_table_source — and synthesizes the results

Exercise C — Generate code using live SAP context

This is the power move — the AI reads your actual SAP system to generate accurate code:

Read the structure of tables EKKO and EKPO from my SAP system. Then write a complete ABAP report that:
1. Has a selection screen for company code and document date range
2. JOINs these two tables using the actual field names you found
3. Displays results in CL_SALV_TABLE
4. Uses modern ABAP syntax
Expected: The AI reads both table structures via MCP, uses the real field names (not guessed ones), and generates a report with correct JOINs
Key Takeaway: Without MCP, you'd need to copy-paste table structures into the chat. With MCP, the AI reads them directly — and the generated code uses actual field names from your system, not hallucinated ones.

Troubleshooting — MCP Lab
The AI doesn't use MCP tools — it just answers from memory
Make sure the MCP server shows as "Connected" in your IDE. If tools are set to "Ask" permission, you need to approve each tool call when prompted.
get_table_contents returns empty
The table might be empty in your system. Try SCARR or SFLIGHT — these are SAP demo tables that usually have data. If using a fresh system, run program SAPBC_DATA_GENERATOR first.
Timeout on large programs
Some SAP standard programs are huge (100K+ lines). Try smaller programs first, or increase the timeout to 120 seconds in your MCP config.
Authorization error on where-used
Where-used analysis requires additional ADT authorizations. Ask your Basis admin to check S_ADT_RES and S_DEVELOP authorization objects.

MCP for SAP ABAP — Connect Your IDE to SAP

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that lets AI assistants (Amazon Q, Kiro, Claude) connect directly to external tools and data sources. For SAP ABAP, this means your AI assistant can read source code, table structures, and data directly from your SAP system — no copy-pasting needed.

Why MCP matters for ABAP developers:
  • Ask "explain program SAPMV45A" → AI reads the source code directly from SAP
  • Ask "what fields are in table VBAK?" → AI queries the table definition live
  • Ask "find all programs that use BAPI_SALESORDER_CREATEFROMDAT2" → AI runs where-used analysis
  • No more copy-pasting code into chat — the AI fetches it automatically

Available MCP Servers for SAP ABAP

Recommended: AWS ABAP Accelerator (official)

In January 2026, AWS launched ABAP Accelerator — an official, purpose-built MCP server for SAP ABAP development that works with Amazon Q Developer and Kiro. It is a free downloadable Docker image that connects to your SAP system via standard ADT, and — critically — integrates directly with the SAP ABAP Test Cockpit (ATC) to validate generated code and dramatically reduce AI "hallucinations". Read the announcement ↗ · GitHub repo ↗

  • Automated ECC → S/4HANA code conversion — converts legacy ABAP while preserving business logic, validated against ATC
  • ATC-validated generation — runs syntax checks, ATC with your custom variants, and object activation; iterates until issues (syntax, security, performance, naming) are resolved
  • Test-Driven Development — generates unit tests to baseline current behavior before changing code, de-risking transformations
  • Clean core development — generates RAP artifacts (CDS views, behavior definitions, service definitions/bindings) and even full Fiori apps from a single prompt
  • Always-current documentation — embeds docs directly in the SAP objects it creates or modifies
  • AI-assisted error resolution — analyzes ST22 dumps, job logs, and error messages to find root causes

Within Kiro CLI, ABAP Accelerator can perform mass code analysis and conversion across many objects at once — ideal for clean core cleanup at scale.

Community MCP Servers (alternatives)

If you cannot run the AWS ABAP Accelerator, two community MCP servers also connect to SAP via ADT (ABAP Development Tools) services:

ServerLanguageAuthKey Features
mcp-abap-adt
GitHub ↗		 Node.js Basic (user/pass) Get programs, classes, functions, tables, table contents, search objects, interfaces, transactions
mcp-adt
GitHub ↗		 Python Basic + BTP (JWT) All of the above + CDS views, metadata extensions, freestyle SQL queries, where-used references, enhancement discovery, BTP support
These are community-maintained open-source projects. Review the code and security implications before connecting to production SAP systems.

Prerequisites

  • SAP system with ADT services enabled (service /sap/bc/adt active in SICF)
  • SAP user with authorization for ADT access
  • Network connectivity from your machine to the SAP system
  • Node.js 18+ (for mcp-abap-adt) or Python 3.9+ (for mcp-adt)

Option A: Setup with VS Code + Amazon Q

Step 1 — Install the MCP server

Choose one of the two servers. We'll use mcp-adt (Python) as it has more features:

git clone https://github.com/YahorNovik/mcp-adt.git
cd mcp-adt
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate    # macOS/Linux
# .venv\Scripts\activate   # Windows
pip install -r requirements.txt

Step 2 — Configure SAP connection

Create a .env file in the mcp-adt directory:

# .env file — replace with your SAP system details
SAP_AUTH_TYPE=basic
SAP_URL=https://your-sap-system:443
SAP_CLIENT=100
SAP_USER=YOUR_USERNAME
SAP_PASS=YOUR_PASSWORD
SAP_VERIFY_SSL=true
Never commit the .env file to Git. Add it to .gitignore immediately.

Step 3 — Add to Amazon Q in VS Code

  1. Open VS Code → Amazon Q panel → Chat → click the tools icon
  2. Click + to add a new MCP server
  3. Select scope: Local (project-specific) or Global
  4. Fill in:
    • Name: sap-abap-adt
    • Transport: stdio
    • Command: python
    • Arguments: /full/path/to/mcp-adt/mcp_server.py
  5. Click Save
  6. Set tool permissions (recommended: Ask for each tool initially)

Or manually edit ~/.aws/amazonq/default.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "sap-abap-adt": {
      "command": "python",
      "args": ["/full/path/to/mcp-adt/mcp_server.py"],
      "timeout": 60
    }
  }
}

Option B: Setup with Kiro

Step 1 — Install the MCP server (same as above)

Follow the same clone + install steps from Option A.

Step 2 — Configure in Kiro

Add the MCP server to your Kiro configuration at ~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "sap-abap-adt": {
      "command": "python",
      "args": ["/full/path/to/mcp-adt/mcp_server.py"],
      "timeout": 60
    }
  }
}

Kiro will auto-detect the MCP tools and make them available in chat.

Option C: Setup with Eclipse (SAP ADT)

Important — Eclipse is different from Kiro and VS Code. MCP is a capability of the AI client, and the Amazon Q plugin for Eclipse does not support MCP servers. There is no mcp.json to configure inside Eclipse, and you cannot add an MCP server through the Eclipse UI. The ~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json (Kiro) and ~/.aws/amazonq/default.json (VS Code) configs shown above do not apply to Eclipse. Instead, Eclipse users run an MCP-capable CLI in a terminal alongside Eclipse.

The pattern for Eclipse developers:

  1. Install the MCP server exactly as in Option A (clone + install, or run the AWS ABAP Accelerator Docker image).
  2. Register the MCP server in a CLI, not in Eclipse — use Kiro CLI or the Amazon Q CLI. The config lives in that CLI's own settings, and the JSON looks the same as the examples above.
  3. Run the CLI in a terminal next to Eclipse: 
    # In a terminal, alongside your Eclipse session
kiro-cli chat        # or the Amazon Q CLI
  4. Keep Eclipse for what it does best — the ABAP editor, native debugging, transport management, and object activation. Use the CLI window for the MCP-powered chat (read source, ATC-validated generation, where-used, clean core artifacts).
  5. Both connect to the same SAP system your Eclipse ADT is pointed at, so they stay in sync.
In short: Kiro and VS Code host MCP inside the IDE. Eclipse does not — you pair it with a CLI. The SAP-side setup (ADT connection, .env / ATC) is identical in all cases; only where you register the MCP server changes.

Troubleshooting

MCP Troubleshooting
MCP server won't connect
Check that the SAP system URL is reachable from your machine. Try curl https://your-sap-system:443/sap/bc/adt/discovery — you should get an XML response. Also verify the /sap/bc/adt service is active in SICF.
Authentication error (401)
Double-check your username, password, and client number in the .env file. If your password contains special characters like #, wrap it in quotes.
Tools show up but return empty results
Your SAP user may lack authorization for ADT services. Ask your Basis admin to check authorizations for the S_ADT_RES authorization object.
Timeout errors on large programs
Increase the timeout in your MCP config from 60 to 120 seconds. Large programs like SAPMV45A can take time to retrieve.
SSL certificate errors
If your SAP system uses self-signed certificates, set SAP_VERIFY_SSL=false in your .env file (not recommended for production).

SAP/ABAP Glossary & Cheat Sheet

Key SAP Terms

TermWhat It Means
ABAPAdvanced Business Application Programming — SAP's proprietary programming language
ALVABAP List Viewer — SAP's standard grid/table display framework
BAPIBusiness Application Programming Interface — standardized API for SAP business objects
BTPBusiness Technology Platform — SAP's cloud platform
CDSCore Data Services — modern data modeling layer using SQL-like views
Clean ABAPSAP's official coding style guide for modern, readable ABAP
Clean CoreSAP's strategy for keeping S/4HANA upgrade-stable and cloud-compliant by extending — not modifying — the core, across six dimensions: software stack, extensibility, integrations, data, processes, operations
CAPCloud Application Programming Model — framework for building side-by-side extensions on SAP BTP
ATCABAP Test Cockpit — SAP's static analysis / code quality checks; used by AWS ABAP Accelerator to validate AI-generated code
ABAP AcceleratorOfficial AWS MCP server (2026) that connects Amazon Q / Kiro to SAP via ADT + ATC for validated code generation, ECC→S/4HANA conversion, and clean core development
MCPModel Context Protocol — open standard that lets AI assistants connect directly to tools and data sources like SAP
Released APIAn SAP object officially released for consumption in extensions — a cornerstone of clean core
ECCERP Central Component — the older SAP ERP system (pre-S/4HANA)
RAPRESTful ABAP Programming Model — modern framework for building OData services
S/4HANASAP's current ERP suite running on HANA database
SAP ADTABAP Development Tools — Eclipse-based IDE for ABAP development
SE80 / SE38Classic SAP transactions for ABAP development (being replaced by ADT)
